question: What are the steps from use case to deployed LLM app, and how do prompting, ICL, RAG, fine-tuning and RLHF differ?
contributions: Lists the adaptation ladder: prompt engineering, in-context learning, RAG, fine-tuning, RLHF
Gives selection criteria for an LLM: task, training data, size, tunability, ecosystem

results.claim: GPT-2 has 117 million parameters; GPT-3 has 175 billion
results.setup: vendor primer's size example for small vs large models
results.note: GPT-2 small is 117M (later restated as 124M); GPT-3 175B is correct.
results.where: section Comparing small and large language models

results.claim: LLMs typically have 10 billion parameters or more
results.where: section Comparing small and large language models

limits: In-context learning is defined as training a model on a data set; it updates no weights.
RLHF is called ongoing, near-real-time fine-tuning; it is an offline stage on fixed preference labels.
Fine-tuning steps omit data quality and PEFT.

figures.caption: A gen AI's encoder and decoder work together to produce accurate outputs.
A word can be identified by the group of words that are used with it frequently. This is the basis for creating vector embeddings.
